name: tar
plain: `tar` bundles many files and folders into one archive file (a tarball) and unpacks them again. With a compression option it also shrinks the archive (.tar.gz, .tar.bz2, .tar.xz).
Challenges ship as tarballs, and it is also how you copy a whole folder tree preserving permissions.
when: List what is inside an archive before extracting it.
Bundle files to move them or keep evidence.

examples.title: Create a compressed archive  (-c -z -f)
examples.cmd: tar -czf site.tar.gz site; ls -l site.tar.gz | awk '{print $5, $9}'

examples.title: List the contents without extracting  (-t)
examples.output:
site/
site/index.html
site/css/
site/css/main.css
site/js/
site/js/app.js
site/uploads/
site/uploads/report.pdf
site/robots.txt
site/.env

examples.title: Verbose listing  (-tv)
examples.output:
drwxr-xr-x itstack/itstack   0 2026-11-23 18:35 site/
-rw-r--r-- itstack/itstack  19 2026-11-10 10:00 site/index.html
drwxr-xr-x itstack/itstack   0 2026-11-23 18:35 site/css/
-rw-r--r-- itstack/itstack   7 2026-11-23 18:35 site/css/main.css

examples.title: Extract into a folder  (-x -C)
examples.cmd: mkdir -p out && tar -xzf site.tar.gz -C out && ls out/site

examples.title: Extract one file  (name after the archive)
Strip leading folders  (--strip-components)
examples.cmd: mkdir -p out2 && tar -xzf site.tar.gz -C out2 --strip-components=1 && ls out2

examples.title: Exclude files  (--exclude)
examples.output:
site/
site/index.html
site/css/
site/css/main.css
site/js/
site/uploads/
site/uploads/report.pdf
site/robots.txt
site/.env

examples.title: Other compressors  (-j, -J, --zstd)
examples.cmd: tar -cjf site.tar.bz2 site && tar -tjf site.tar.bz2 | head -2

examples.title: Let tar guess the compression  (-a)
examples.cmd: tar -caf site.tar.xz site && file site.tar.xz | cut -c1-60
examples.output: site.tar.xz: XZ compressed data, checksum CRC64

mistakes: Forgetting -f or putting options after the archive name: -f must be followed directly by the file name (tar -czf a.tgz dir).
Extracting an untrusted tar as root: names like ../ or absolute paths can overwrite files; list first with -t.
Unpacking into the current folder with no top-level directory (a tar bomb): check with tar -tf first.
Mixing up -c (create) and -x (extract) when pasting commands.
Using -z on an archive that is not gzip: use tar -xf and let tar detect, or check with file.
